contentFull:
What can you expect from this year’s Eurotier?

Artificial intelligence, automation and precision livestock technologies are shaping the future of animal production, a trend clearly reflected in the EuroTier 2026 Innovation Awards. While the awards span all livestock sectors, a few of this year’s winners stand out for offering clear benefits to poultry producers. 

Sunita van Es-SahotaEditor Poultry World

Oct 26

News

Snapshot of Eurotier 2024. This year’s edition will focus on intelligence in animal farming. Photo: DLG 

The 2026 edition of EuroTier will take place in Hanover, Germany, from 10-13 November. Speaking at a press conference in Offenbach, Germany, organiser DLG (German Agricultural Society) announced that more than 2,100 exhibitors from 55 countries will participate in this year’s event. 

Under the theme 'Intelligence in animal farming', EuroTier will focus on key topics including animal health and welfare, housing systems, feeding technology and forage production. As the world’s leading trade fair for livestock professionals, the event aims to address current market pressures and structural changes through innovative technologies, practical expertise and forward-looking management concepts. 

According to DLG CEO Dr Lothar Hövelmann, entrepreneurial competence is becoming increasingly important for livestock businesses operating in challenging markets. Drawing on performance analyses from DLG benchmark networks, he noted that the poultry sector continues to benefit from generally positive market prospects. 

In the global egg sector, however, avian influenza continues to create volatility by rapidly affecting flock numbers and supply, helping to keep egg prices high in many regions. Global broiler production is also expected to maintain strong growth momentum of around 2.5%, supported by chicken meat’s competitive price position, although avian influenza and geopolitical developments remain key risk factors.

Spotlight and expert stages

Ines Rathke, show director of EuroTier 2026, outlined what visitors can expect from this year’s event: “EuroTier 2026 is the world’s platform for the global livestock sector. It brings together the key decisionmakers of today and tomorrow.” 

Feed and feeding remain central themes, encompassing feed production, feed management and strategies to meet animals’ nutritional requirements. Forage production will also feature prominently in the technical programme. 

Rathke highlighted 7 themed “Spotlights” and a range of new expert stages across the exhibition grounds. “Over the 4 days of EuroTier, numerous stages will host dedicated programmes throughout the halls, in addition to side events such as the Startup Sprints and numerous networking opportunities,” she said. 

The Spotlights will give exhibitors a plat form to showcase new technologies; visitors can gain firsthand experience of automation solutions and engage with livestock veterinarians and industry experts. A total of 9 specialist stages will provide dedicated content on topics including poultry, pigs, dairy, biosecurity and feed safety. 

In addition, a live charity auction will allow visitors to bid on innovative products while supporting charitable causes. Misset titles Poultry World, All About Feed, Pig Progress and Dairy Global will contribute to the expert stage programme with seminars covering topics such as feed efficiency, gut health, sustainability, animal welfare and emission reduction.

Animal welfare award

Two innovations received the Animal Welfare Award 2026 as part of the Innovation Award EuroTier 2026 scheme. WEDA Dammann & Westerkamp and VetVise were recognised for their Smart Farrowing Pen, which combines AI-supported animal monitoring with automated climate and feeding control. The second award went to Lock SmartSolutions and smaXtec for SmartCalving, a system that uses bolus-based animal data to automatically optimise the calving environment for both cow and calf. 

Gold and silver award winners

The medal-winning innovations represented 10 countries and territories across Asia, Europe and North America and spanned 14 product categories. While many of this year’s awards recognised advances in AI, automation and precision livestock technologies for the dairy and pig sectors, the poultry sector also secured recognition with the following innovations:

Egg breakage detection technology

Bröring Technology, hall 14, C44The Electronic Egg is a reusable diagnostic data logger that helps identify the causes of egg damage in automated transport and processing systems. Designed to match the size, shape and weight of a real egg, it moves through production lines alongside commercial eggs while recording shocks, vibrations, rotations and impacts in real time. An integrated LED warning system provides immediate feedback on critical transfer points and handling areas, enabling operators to quickly identify and correct problems. By pinpointing sources of excessive impact, the system helps reduce egg breakage and improve egg handling and transport efficiency.

Autonomous mobile poultry barn

UKKÖ Robotics, hall 17, D45The Rovabarn is a highly auto mated mobile poultry barn designed for off-grid egg production. Powered by solar energy and onboard battery storage, the unit can move independently up to 20 times per day, giving birds continuous access to fresh pasture while helping to distribute nutrients more evenly across the land. Farmers can monitor feed and water consumption, energy use and barn movements through a mobile app, while automated folding walls regulate the indoor climate. Advanced predator protection systems further support bird welfare and security.

LiDAR-based feed silo LiDAR-based feed silo monitoring

Constantec Co., Ltd., hall 12, B03

Feed Check is an automated monitoring system that measures both feed inventory and stor age conditions inside agricultural silos. Using high-precision LiDAR technology, it creates a 3D map of the feed surface to calculate remaining feed volumes more accurately than conventional point measurements. Integrated temperature and humidity sensors also help monitor feed quality, providing early warning of conditions that could affect feed safety and performance. Designed for wire-free operation, the system combines low energy consumption with up to 5 years of battery life.
translationZh:
人工智能、自动化和精准畜牧技术正在塑造动物生产的未来，这一趋势在EuroTier 2026创新奖中得到了清晰体现。虽然奖项涵盖所有畜牧领域，但今年有几项获奖者对家禽生产者具有明显益处。

2026年EuroTier将于11月10日至13日在德国汉诺威举行。主办方DLG（德国农业协会）在德国奥芬巴赫举行的新闻发布会上宣布，今年将有来自55个国家的2100多家参展商参加。

以“动物养殖智能化”为主题，EuroTier将聚焦动物健康与福利、栏舍系统、饲喂技术和饲草生产等关键议题。作为全球领先的畜牧专业人士贸易展会，该活动旨在通过创新技术、实用专业知识和前瞻性管理理念来应对当前的市场压力和结构性变化。

DLG首席执行官Lothar Hövelmann博士表示，在充满挑战的市场中，畜牧企业的经营能力正变得越来越重要。他援引DLG基准网络的绩效分析指出，家禽行业继续受益于总体积极的市场前景。

然而，在全球蛋品行业，禽流感继续通过快速影响鸡群数量和供应来制造波动，帮助许多地区维持高蛋价。全球肉鸡产量预计也将保持约2.5%的强劲增长势头，这得益于鸡肉具有竞争力的价格定位，但禽流感和地缘政治发展仍是关键风险因素。

**焦点展区和专家舞台**

EuroTier 2026展会总监Ines Rathke介绍了今年活动的看点：“EuroTier 2026是全球畜牧业的全球平台。它汇聚了当今和未来的关键决策者。”

饲料与饲喂仍是核心主题，涵盖饲料生产、饲料管理以及满足动物营养需求的策略。饲草生产也将在技术议程中占据重要位置。

Rathke重点介绍了分布在展览场地各处的7个主题“焦点展区”和一系列新的专家舞台。她表示：“在EuroTier的4天里，除了创业冲刺和众多交流机会等配套活动外，众多舞台将在各展馆全天候举办专题节目。”

焦点展区将为参展商提供展示新技术的平台；参观者可以亲身体验自动化解决方案，并与畜牧兽医和行业专家交流。总共9个专业舞台将提供包括家禽、猪、奶牛、生物安全和饲料安全等主题的专门内容。

此外，一场现场慈善拍卖将让参观者竞拍创新产品，同时支持慈善事业。Misset旗下刊物Poultry World、All About Feed、Pig Progress和Dairy Global将通过研讨会为专家舞台节目做出贡献，涵盖饲料效率、肠道健康、可持续性、动物福利和减排等主题。

**动物福利奖**

两项创新获得了EuroTier 2026创新奖计划中的2026年动物福利奖。WEDA Dammann & Westerkamp和VetVise因其智能产仔栏获得认可，该产品将AI支持的动物监测与自动化气候和饲喂控制相结合。第二个奖项授予Lock SmartSolutions和smaXtec的SmartCalving系统，该系统利用基于瘤胃 bolus 的动物数据自动优化母牛和犊牛的产犊环境。

**金奖和银奖获得者**

获奖创新代表了亚洲、欧洲和北美的10个国家和地区，涵盖14个产品类别。虽然今年许多奖项认可了奶牛和猪领域在AI、自动化和精准畜牧技术方面的进步，但家禽行业也凭借以下创新获得了认可：

**鸡蛋破损检测技术**

Bröring Technology，14号馆，C44展位。Electronic Egg是一种可重复使用的诊断数据记录器，有助于识别自动化运输和加工系统中鸡蛋破损的原因。其设计在大小、形状和重量上与真实鸡蛋相匹配，随商品蛋一起通过生产线，同时实时记录冲击、振动、旋转和碰撞。集成的LED预警系统对关键转运点和处理区域提供即时反馈，使操作人员能够快速识别并纠正问题。通过精确定位过度冲击的来源，该系统有助于减少鸡蛋破损，提高鸡蛋处理和运输效率。

**自主移动禽舍**

UKKÖ Robotics，17号馆，D45展位。Rovabarn是一款高度自动化的移动禽舍，专为离网鸡蛋生产而设计。由太阳能和车载电池储能供电，该单元每天可独立移动多达20次，使鸡群持续获得新鲜牧草，同时帮助更均匀地将养分分布到土地上。农民可以通过移动应用程序监测饲料和水的消耗、能源使用和禽舍移动情况，自动折叠墙调节室内气候。先进的捕食者防护系统进一步支持禽鸟福利和安全。

**基于LiDAR的饲料料仓监测**

Constantec Co., Ltd.，12号馆，B03展位。Feed Check是一种自动化监测系统，可测量农业料仓内的饲料库存和储存条件。利用高精度LiDAR技术，它创建饲料表面的3D地图，比传统点测量更准确地计算剩余饲料量。集成的温湿度传感器还有助于监测饲料质量，对可能影响饲料安全和性能的条件提供早期预警。该系统专为无线操作而设计，结合低能耗和长达5年的电池寿命。
author: Sunita van Es-Sahota
